artiest/100-gecs.text:
100 gecs is an American duo made up of Dylan Brady and Laura Les, who started out in 2015 in the St. Louis area. They first made music together in the winter of 2015, in Laura's apartment in Chicago, and released their first EP themselves in 2016. They have told several contradictory stories about where the name comes from. A breakthrough came in 2019, when they played a DJ set together at the Minecraft Fire Festival and then carried on writing.

The debut album 1000 gecs was released in May 2019 to positive reviews. One critic called it hyperpop in its most extreme form: trap beats processed almost to destruction, exaggerated emo singing and streams of lightning-fast arpeggios. In 2020 came the remix album 1000 gecs and the Tree of Clues, with contributions from A. G. Cook, Charli XCX and Injury Reserve, among others. That same year they signed to Atlantic Records. The second album, 10,000 gecs, appeared in 2023. Brady also produced for other artists, such as Rico Nasty.

Their music is wild and yet catchy. Styles collide within a few seconds: ska, metal, trap, dance and pop. In doing so they helped shape the genre of hyperpop, which in the 2020s had a major influence on young pop makers.
artiest/100-gecs.listen: Listen to Money Machine, the track that A. G. Cook remixed in 2019, and notice how quickly the sounds change. Try counting how many different styles you hear in a single minute.

artiest/2-unlimited.text:
2 Unlimited was a Eurodance act with Dutch faces and Belgian creators. The producers Jean-Paul De Coster and Phil Wilde started the project in Antwerp in 1991 and released the records on the Belgian label Byte Records. For the vocals, the stage and the videos they chose two Dutch performers: rapper Ray Slijngaard and singer Anita Doth. The public saw Ray and Anita, but the music was made in the studio of Wilde and De Coster.

The first single, Get Ready for This (1991), reached number two in England and Australia. In 1993 came No Limit, which went to number 1 in ten countries, including the Netherlands and England. The formula was simple and effective: a hard beat, a short synthesizer riff, rap in the verses and a chorus that consists almost entirely of the title. The albums Get Ready! (1992), No Limits! (1993) and Real Things (1994) followed. In England the records came out through PWL Continental, a label from the circle around Stock Aitken Waterman.

In April 1996 Ray and Anita left, after disagreements over the musical direction and over money. A new line-up with Romy van Ooijen and Marjon van Iwaarden made the album II in 1998, but gave up in 1999. Since 2009 Slijngaard and Doth have performed together again. According to AllMusic, 2 Unlimited sold eighteen million records worldwide. The project shows how Eurodance worked: producers built the songs and only then looked for faces to go with them, just like the hit factories of London.
artiest/2-unlimited.listen: In No Limit, listen for the short synthesizer riff that keeps coming back, and for the break halfway through, where everything drops away except the beat. Then compare the British version: there, Ray's rap is largely cut out, and the track still works.

artiest/2pac.text:
Tupac Shakur, known as a rapper as 2Pac, was born in East Harlem, New York, in 1971. His mother Afeni Shakur was a member of the Black Panther Party. He took classes in drama, poetry and jazz at the Baltimore School for the Arts and moved to Marin City in California in 1988. He became one of the best-known rappers of the 1990s, as a storyteller about life in the neighbourhood and as the focal point of the feud between the East Coast and the West Coast.

He took his first steps with the group Digital Underground. His own debut, 2Pacalypse Now, came out in 1991. Me Against the World (1995) went to number 1 on the Billboard 200 while he was in prison. Suge Knight of Death Row Records paid his bail, and 2Pac signed to that label. His first single there was California Love (1995), produced by Dr. Dre with Roger Troutman on the chorus. In 1996 the track spent two weeks at number 1 on the Hot 100. All Eyez on Me (1996), a double album, entered at number 1 straight away.

Besides music, he acted in films such as Juice (1992) and Poetic Justice (1993), with Janet Jackson. The rivalry with The Notorious B.I.G. and his label Bad Boy ran high, notably through the track Hit 'Em Up. In September 1996 2Pac was shot in Las Vegas. He died six days later, aged 25. After his death his work continued to appear. In 2017, in the first year he was eligible, he was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
artiest/2pac.listen: In California Love, Roger Troutman sings the chorus through a talk box: the sound comes from a synthesizer and is shaped into words with his mouth. Also notice the hook, which goes back, via a sample of EPMD, to Woman to Woman by Joe Cocker.

artiest/808-state.text:
808 State is an English electronic group, founded in Manchester in 1987 by Graham Massey, Martin Price and Gerald Simpson. The name comes from the Roland TR-808 drum machine and from the shared state of mind of its members. Price owned the influential record shop Eastern Bloc Records and started the independent label Creed. The three began as a hip hop group, Hit Squad Manchester, and switched to acid house. In 1988, over a weekend in January at Spirit Studios in Manchester, they recorded their debut Newbuild, which came out in September.

The breakthrough came in 1989 when BBC Radio 1 DJ Gary Davies picked up the track Pacific State. It spent eleven weeks in the British chart and reached number ten. Simpson left that year to go solo as A Guy Called Gerald, and became embroiled in a legal dispute with the band over the writing credits. After Newbuild and Ninety in 1989 came Ex:el in 1991, Gorgeous in 1993, Don Solaris in 1996 and Outpost Transmission in 2002. The group also recorded an acid house version of Blue Monday by New Order, which was not released until 2004.

Their early work influenced the emerging acid house scene in England. AllMusic called the group one of the most important dance acts of all time, with an influence on techno and alternative dance music. Aphex Twin found the sound colder and at the same time more human than Chicago acid.
artiest/808-state.listen: Listen to Pacific. Notice the soft synthesizer lines and the saxophone above the calm, steady rhythm of the drum machine.

artiest/a-g-cook.text:
A. G. Cook, born Alexander Guy Cook in 1990, is an English producer. He is the son of two architects and studied music at Goldsmiths in London. There he played with his friend Danny L Harle in the project Dux Content, which experimented with rhythms and time signatures. In 2013 he founded the label PC Music, which set out to bring in people who do not usually make music and treated them like artists on a major record label.

His first solo single, Keri Baby from 2014, uses pop clichés and distorted voices to make singer Hannah Diamond sound like a digital figure on a screen. Beautiful, from the same year, is a parody of Eurodance, with high, pitch-shifted voices. With Sophie he made Hey QT. Later he became executive producer for Charli XCX, on the albums Charli and How I'm Feeling Now, among others, as well as Brat. For Brat he won a Grammy. In 2022 he contributed to a track on Beyoncé's Renaissance. His own albums are 7G and Apple from 2020 and Britpop from 2024.

The exaggerated pop sounds of PC Music became the foundation of hyperpop, a genre that Cook developed and popularised. In doing so he showed that an artificial, almost mocking pop style can move you just as much as the real thing.
artiest/a-g-cook.listen: Listen to Beautiful and notice the wound-up voice and the squeaking, bubbling sounds. See whether you hear the track as a joke, or whether it sweeps you along against your will.

artiest/a-ha.text:
a-ha was formed in Oslo in 1982 by guitarist Pål Waaktaar, keyboard player Magne Furuholmen and singer Morten Harket. Waaktaar and Furuholmen had previously played together in the band Bridges. The trio moved to London to look for a record deal. a-ha shows how in the 1980s the synthesizer took the place of the guitar, and how a music video could make a hit.

Take On Me had a long run-up. An early version was called Lesson One. The first single, produced by Tony Mansfield in 1984, failed to catch on. In 1985 the band recorded the song again with producer Alan Tarney. On the record you hear synthesizers such as the Roland Juno-60, the PPG Wave and the Yamaha DX7, with a LinnDrum as the drum machine. The breakthrough came with the video by director Steve Barron, in which drawn and filmed images flow into one another thanks to rotoscoping. In October 1985 Take On Me went to number 1 on the Billboard Hot 100; in England it reached number 2. The debut album Hunting High and Low (1985) reached number 1 in Norway.

At the MTV Video Music Awards of 1986 the video won six awards. The Sun Always Shines on T.V. became the band's only British number 1. In 1987 a-ha made The Living Daylights, the title song of the James Bond film of the same name. The group split in 2010 and returned in 2015 with the album Cast in Steel. In 2020 the Take On Me video passed a billion views on YouTube, more than thirty years after it was made.
artiest/a-ha.listen: Take On Me (1985): listen to the riff in the intro, a fierce synthesizer sound above a drum machine. At the end of the chorus, notice Morten Harket, who climbs on in falsetto to the highest note of the song, an E5.

artiest/a-r-kane.text:
A.R. Kane was an English duo of Alex Ayuli and Rudy Tambala, who had known each other since primary school in East London. Ayuli is of Nigerian descent and, as a teenager, played in a dub sound system; Tambala, with a Malawian father and an English mother, came from the jazz-funk scene. A television appearance by Cocteau Twins inspired them. At a party in 1986 Tambala made up the story that the two of them played in a band together. A week later a record label phoned, and the duo quickly made a demo without a drummer, with a guitar and two cassette recorders.

The first single, When You're Sad, came out in 1986. It was followed on the label 4AD by the EP Lollita, produced by Robin Guthrie of Cocteau Twins. Label boss Ivo Watts-Russell brought them together with the group Colourbox and a few DJs. Under the name M|A|R|R|S they made Pump Up the Volume in 1987, which went to number 1 in England. The debut album 69 (1988) and its successor i (1989) topped the independent chart. After New Clear Child (1994) the duo split up.

A.R. Kane blended echoing, distorted guitars with dub production, drum machines, free jazz and studio experiments. Ayuli himself coined the term dream pop for it. The duo then faded into obscurity, but critics regard it as one of the most innovative groups of the 1980s, with an influence on shoegaze, trip hop and post-rock. They also broke the stereotype that Black musicians made only soul, reggae or hip hop.
artiest/a-r-kane.listen: Listen to Pump Up the Volume by M|A|R|R|S and notice how the track is built from samples: loose snippets of voice and music from other records, over a continuous dance beat. Hear how the cut-and-paste technique from hip hop becomes dance music here.

artiest/a-r-rahman.text: A.R. Rahman (born in Chennai in 1967) began as a keyboard player, including in the orchestra of Ilaiyaraaja, and made advertising jingles. Director Mani Ratnam gave him his first film in 1992: Roja. Rahman worked from his own studio and built up his music layer by layer, with synthesizers, samples, acoustic instruments and singers from all over India. It sounded clearer and more international than Indian film music had until then. Bombay (1995), Dil Se.. (1998) and Lagaan (2001) followed, among others. With Slumdog Millionaire (2008) he won two Oscars, for the score and for the song Jai Ho.
artiest/a-r-rahman.listen: Notice the layered studio production: electronic beats and synthesizers alongside Indian percussion, chorus and solo vocals.

artiest/a-r-rahman-sukhwinder-singh-en-s.text:
Chaiyya Chaiyya comes from Dil Se.., a 1998 Hindi film by director Mani Ratnam. Three names stand behind the song. A. R. Rahman composed the music, one of India's best-known film composers, who often worked with Mani Ratnam. Sukhwinder Singh sang the lead vocal, together with Sapna Awasthi.

Sukhwinder Singh was born in 1971 in Amritsar in the Punjab. As a boy he did athletics, but then music won out over sprinting. He took singing lessons with the Punjabi musician B. S. Narang and began a career in music at seventeen. First he worked as an arranger for the composer duo Laxmikant and Pyarelal and sang in choruses. As a playback singer, someone who records the songs for actors who only lip-sync on screen, he gained wide recognition thanks to Chaiyya Chaiyya. For it he won the Filmfare Award for Best Male Playback Singer.

In Indian film the singing belongs to the story, but the singers stay out of sight. The public often knows the songs better than the actors who sing them on screen. Singh later also worked on Jai Ho from Slumdog Millionaire, which won an Oscar for best original song in 2009. In this way the sound of Bollywood, in the hands of Rahman and his singers, travelled far beyond India.
artiest/a-r-rahman-sukhwinder-singh-en-s.listen: Listen to Chaiyya Chaiyya and notice how the singing voice and the rhythm keep urging each other on. Can you hear how the voice follows the rhythm of the song?

artiest/a-tribe-called-quest.text:
A Tribe Called Quest was an American hip hop group from Queens, New York, formed in 1985. Rapper and producer Q-Tip and rapper Phife Dawg were childhood friends. With DJ Ali Shaheed Muhammad and rapper Jarobi White they made demos on beats that Q-Tip pieced together with a cassette deck. They got their name in 1988 from the Jungle Brothers. Together with that group, De La Soul and Queen Latifah they formed the collective Native Tongues: rappers with a positive message, an interest in African roots and a broad taste in samples.

The debut People's Instinctive Travels and the Paths of Rhythm (1990) was playful, with samples from jazz, funk, soul and rock and tracks such as Can I Kick It? and Bonita Applebum. On The Low End Theory (1991) jazz really moved to the centre. The production was bare: voice, drums and bass, with a relaxed atmosphere drawn from bebop and hard bop. Jazz bassist Ron Carter played double bass on Verses from the Abstract. Q-Tip and Phife Dawg now rapped in turns, and that interplay became their trademark. Midnight Marauders (1993) brought Award Tour and Electric Relaxation.

After Beats, Rhymes and Life (1996) and The Love Movement (1998) the group split up. In 2016 one more album appeared, with contributions from Phife Dawg, who had died shortly before. A Tribe Called Quest is regarded as one of the pioneers of jazz rap and alternative hip hop, and also inspired neo-soul. In 2024 the group was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
artiest/a-tribe-called-quest.listen: Listen to Verses from the Abstract from 1991. Notice the warm double bass of jazz musician Ron Carter beneath the bare drums, and how calmly Q-Tip raps over it.

artiest/aaliyah.text:
Aaliyah Dana Haughton was born on 16 January 1979 in Brooklyn, New York, and grew up in Detroit. Her mother sang, and Aaliyah had singing lessons from an early age. At ten she appeared on the television programme Star Search and shared the stage with Gladys Knight. At twelve she signed a record contract.

Her debut album Age Ain't Nothing but a Number came out in 1994 and was written and produced by R. Kelly. After reports of an unlawful marriage to him she broke her contract and moved to Atlantic. For her second album, One in a Million (1996), she worked with producer Timbaland and writer Missy Elliott. Together they made R&B with stuttering, unusual rhythms and a lot of space in the music. In 2000 she played her first film role, in Romeo Must Die. The track Try Again from that film became a number 1 on the American Billboard Hot 100. In 2001 her third album, Aaliyah, appeared, with Rock the Boat and More Than a Woman, among others.

Aaliyah sang lightly and smoothly, almost casually, over rhythms that were angular and innovative. She is regarded as one of the artists who gave modern R&B, pop and hip hop a new shape in the late 1990s. On 25 August 2001 she was killed in a plane crash in the Bahamas, only 22 years old. Her music continued to be successful afterwards.
artiest/aaliyah.listen: Listen to Try Again (2000), produced by Timbaland. Notice the stuttering, irregular rhythm and the strange electronic sounds, and how calmly and smoothly Aaliyah sings over them.

artiest/aaron-copland.text: Aaron Copland was born in Brooklyn in 1900, studied in Paris with Nadia Boulanger and was already a well-known concert composer when he began writing for film. He started with the documentary The City (1939). Of Mice and Men (1939) and Our Town (1940) followed. Copland resisted the thick, continuous orchestral sound of Hollywood. He wrote transparent music with open fourths and fifths, simple melodies and plenty of space between the instruments. This is how the American countryside came to sound. For The Heiress (1949) he won an Oscar. He turned The Red Pony (1949) into an orchestral suite. His film style became the model for Western music and for the 'American' film sound in general.
artiest/aaron-copland.listen: Notice the open harmonies and the empty space between high and low instruments: this is how the feeling of a wide landscape arises.

artiest/ab-baars.text:
Ab Baars was born in 1955 in Axel, in Zeeland, and is a saxophonist and clarinettist in improvised music. He had piano lessons at five and played tenor saxophone at fifteen. He studied at the conservatoire in Rotterdam, where he explored classical music as well as jazz and rock. In 1989 he took clarinet lessons with John Carter in Los Angeles on a grant, and his 1997 album A Free Step contains music by Carter that had not been heard before.

As a student Baars played in Orkest de Volharding and got to know people with whom he would often collaborate later, such as Ig Henneman, Guus Janssen, Misha Mengelberg and Wolter Wierbos. In 1986 he joined the ICP Orchestra. In 1989 he founded a trio with bassist Wilbert de Joode and drummer Martin van Duynhoven, and later invited Roswell Rudd as a guest. Since 1989 he has occasionally performed with the Dutch punk band The Ex. He recorded Hef, Sliptong and Cement, among others, with his own duo with Henneman.

Baars is an important voice in Dutch improvised music. He shows how jazz, contemporary composition and punk energy could coexist in the Netherlands, and how the saxophone and clarinet sound full of character within that mix.
artiest/ab-baars.listen: Listen to a recording of his trio and notice how saxophone or clarinet, bass and drums answer one another as equals. Try to hear who takes the lead and when that changes.

artiest/abba.text:
ABBA is a Swedish pop group, formed in Stockholm in 1972 by two couples: Agnetha Fältskog and Björn Ulvaeus, and Anni-Frid Lyngstad and Benny Andersson. The two women sang, the two men wrote and produced. ABBA proved that a group from outside England and America could conquer the world market, and made Sweden a country of hit writers.

On 6 April 1974 ABBA won the Eurovision Song Contest in Brighton with Waterloo. It became their first number 1, in nine European countries, including England. Sound engineer Michael B. Tretow gave the group a clear studio sound, in which parts were doubled as in Phil Spector's Wall of Sound, but in which every instrument remained audible. Dancing Queen (1976), from the album Arrival, became a number 1 in the United States and fifteen other countries. For the dance rhythm, Andersson and Ulvaeus took inspiration from Rock Your Baby by George McCrae. In 1978 the group converted an old cinema in Stockholm into the Polar Music Studio. After The Visitors (1981) ABBA split up at the end of 1982.

The music stayed popular afterwards. The compilation album ABBA Gold (1992) became a worldwide bestseller, the musical Mamma Mia! premiered in 1999 and was made into a film in 2008. In 2021 Voyage appeared, the first new album in forty years. Since 2022 digital avatars of the four have performed in a purpose-built venue in London. After ABBA, Sweden built a hit industry, with Max Martin among others.
artiest/abba.listen: Dancing Queen (1976) does not begin with the verse but in the middle of the chorus, with the line "You can dance". Notice how the song thus starts at its strongest point, and how clearly piano, strings and voices sit side by side.

artiest/abbey-lincoln.text: Abbey Lincoln began as a nightclub singer and appeared in a Hollywood film in 1956. Billie Holiday was her great example. Through her relationship with drummer Max Roach, whom she married, she became involved in the civil rights movement. On We Insist! (1960) she sang and screamed in the section Protest, a piece without words. Her own album Straight Ahead (1961) was rejected by some critics because she was said to be too political. She also acted in films, including For Love of Ivy (1968). In the 1990s she made a series of albums of her own songs for the label Verve, which made her widely known again.
artiest/abbey-lincoln.listen: Hear how the voice does not just sing, but also protests and screams.

artiest/abc.text:
ABC is an English pop band from Sheffield, formed in 1980. The band grew out of the electronic outfit Vice Versa of Stephen Singleton and Mark White. Martin Fry, who made a fanzine, interviewed them and was asked shortly afterwards to join. At the end of 1980 Fry became the singer and the group was called ABC. Singleton played saxophone, White guitar and keyboards. Fry is the only member who has always been part of it.

The first single, Tears Are Not Enough, came out in 1981. In 1982 followed the debut album The Lexicon of Love, produced by Trevor Horn, which went to number 1 in Great Britain. Poison Arrow, The Look of Love and All of My Heart became hits. ABC belonged to the new pop of the early 1980s, bands that after punk sought glamour and grand gestures again. The music blended synth-pop with disco and rock, with lush strings arranged by Anne Dudley, who also played keyboards on them. Fry sang with great drama about heartbreak and appeared in photographs in a gold suit.

The follow-up Beauty Stab (1983) sounded rougher and did less well. With How to Be a ... Zillionaire! (1985) ABC scored in America with Be Near Me, and Alphabet City (1987) included When Smokey Sings, a tribute to Smokey Robinson. In those years Fry also had cancer and recovered. ABC kept performing, and in 2016 The Lexicon of Love II appeared, a sequel to the famous debut.
artiest/abc.listen: Listen to The Look of Love from 1982. Notice the danceable disco rhythms, the lush strings and how theatrically Martin Fry delivers the lyrics.

artiest/abdel-halim-hafez.text:
Abdel Halim Hafez was born Abdel Halim Ali Shabana in 1929 in El-Halawat, in the Egyptian province of Sharqia, north of Cairo. His mother died shortly after his birth and his father a few months later. He grew up in an orphanage and later with relatives in Cairo. He learned music from his older brother, went to the Arabic Music Institute at fourteen and studied as an oboist at the music institute.

His breakthrough came in 1953. At the last moment he stepped in for a singer who could not perform in a live radio broadcast. Hafez Abdel Wahab, who ran the music programmes of Egyptian radio, heard him, and Halim took his first name as his stage name. At first people found his new way of singing strange; later he became a singer whom all generations could appreciate. With composer Mohammed Abdel Wahab he made many love songs, such as Ahwak and Fatet Ganbena. With the poet Mohamed Hamza he made Zay el Hawa and Sawah, among others. He also sang many patriotic songs and acted in sixteen films.

He worked mainly as a live singer and therefore rarely released a studio album. He himself played the oboe, piano, oud and guitar, among other instruments, and took part in composing his songs. He died in 1977 in London of liver failure. His funeral drew tens of thousands of people. Decades later his songs were still heard during the Egyptian revolution of 2011, and a snippet of Khosara turned up in 1999 in Big Pimpin by Jay-Z.
artiest/abdel-halim-hafez.listen: Listen to Qareat El Fengan and notice how the voice carries the melody and how the orchestra responds behind it. Notice how the singer lets the long lines ring out.

artiest/abdullah-ibrahim.text: Abdullah Ibrahim, first known as Dollar Brand, grew up in Cape Town with church music, marabi and American jazz; Duke Ellington and Thelonious Monk became his models. In 1959 he formed The Jazz Epistles with Hugh Masekela and Kippie Moeketsi. After apartheid was tightened he left in 1962 with singer Sathima Bea Benjamin for Zürich. There Ellington heard his trio and arranged a recording. In 1968 he became a Muslim and took the name Abdullah Ibrahim. On a visit to Cape Town in 1974 he recorded Mannenberg, which became a song of resistance. His music blends hymns, Cape rhythms and jazz. He died in 2026.
artiest/abdullah-ibrahim.listen: Hear the repeated, hymn-like chord sequence above which the saxophone sings.

artiest/abe-schwartz.text:
Abe Schwartz was born in 1881 near Bucharest in Romania and was a klezmer violinist, composer and bandleader. Around 1900 he emigrated with his parents to the United States. His father, a tinsmith, tried to talk him out of a musician's life. In New York in the 1900s and 1910s he led dance bands. During the First World War he played in the restaurant Little Bessarabia. In 1917 Columbia Records hired him to record instrumental music by immigrant groups and to find new Jewish talent.

In those years Schwartz led dozens of recordings, with musicians he hired for the session. Among them were the clarinettists Naftule Brandwein and Dave Tarras, two of the greatest klezmer musicians of the last century. He often worked without written arrangements, so that the playing sounded free, spontaneous and a little untidy. In 1919 he published his first song and also made records under pseudonyms. In 1920 he had about thirty-five pieces registered with the Library of Congress. His best-known melody, Di Grine Kuzine, is still played today. Ikh bin a Boarder bay mayn vayb followed in 1941. He died in 1963.

For the history of pop, Schwartz matters because he made sure that klezmer, the dance music of Eastern European Jews, was captured on record. His recordings are an important source for the klezmer revival of later decades.
artiest/abe-schwartz.listen: Listen to Di Grine Kuzine and notice the clarinet or violin that makes the melody weep and laugh at once with its sobs and ornaments. Can you hear the dance music underneath?

artiest/abe-schwartz-orchestra-en-naftul.text:
Abe Schwartz was born in 1881 near Bucharest in Romania and emigrated around 1900 with his parents to the United States. In New York he worked as a violinist and leader of dance orchestras, among other Romanian klezmer leaders. In 1917 an A&R man from Columbia Records brought him into the studio, and from that moment he recorded klezmer and music for the Yiddish theatre for decades. He was a composer, violinist and bandleader all at once.

His orchestras captured many of the best klezmer musicians of the early twentieth century, including Dave Tarras and the clarinettist Naftule Brandwein. In 1920 he had about thirty-five pieces registered with the Library of Congress. His best-known melody is Di Grine Kuzine, which is still played today and has had imitators. In 1923 Brandwein left the orchestra to start a group of his own on a rival label. Schloimke Beckerman took his place. Later Schwartz also helped found the Boiberiker Kapelye, which was heard on the radio and on record for five years. He retired in the 1950s and died in the Bronx in 1963.

The recordings of Schwartz and Brandwein show how the music of Jewish immigrants from Eastern Europe gained a second life in New York. They are dance music and lament in one, played on violin and clarinet, and they form the basis of klezmer as it was later rediscovered.
artiest/abe-schwartz-orchestra-en-naftul.listen: Listen to Firn di mekhutonim aheym and notice how violin and clarinet ornament the melody. Try to hear whether it is a dance or rather a song.

artiest/abel-meeropol.text:
Abel Meeropol was born in 1903 in the Bronx, in New York, the son of Jewish immigrants from Ukraine. He took a bachelor's degree at City College and a master's at Harvard and taught English at a secondary school for seventeen years, where James Baldwin was one of his pupils. He published his poems and songs under the pseudonym Lewis Allan, in memory of his two stillborn children.

In 1937 he wrote the poem Strange Fruit, an indictment of lynchings, which first appeared as Bitter Fruit in a trade union magazine for teachers. Later he set it to music himself. The song was recorded by Billie Holiday and later sung by Nina Simone. Holiday wrote in her book that she had helped make the music, but biographers dispute that. Meeropol wrote much more, including The House I Live In, a hit for Frank Sinatra and Josh White, and Apples, Peaches and Cherries, a hit for Peggy Lee. He also wrote the libretto of the opera The Good Soldier Schweik by Robert Kurka.

Meeropol was a member of the American Communist Party from 1932 to 1947. He and his wife Anne adopted the two sons of Julius and Ethel Rosenberg after their parents had been executed. Strange Fruit is regarded as one of the first protest songs in the history of pop, full of suppressed anger and harrowing images.
artiest/abel-meeropol.listen: Listen to Strange Fruit in the recording by Billie Holiday and notice how slowly and restrainedly she sings. Notice how little accompaniment there is beneath her voice and what effect that has on the words.

artiest/abida-parveen.text:
Abida Parveen is a Pakistani singer who is often called the queen of Sufi music. She was born in 1954 in Larkana, in the province of Sindh, into a Sufi family. Her father, Ustad Ghulam Haider, was a singer and music teacher. He trained her and chose her as his musical heir over his two sons. Later she also had lessons from Ustad Salamat Ali Khan. As a child she was already singing at the shrines of Sufi saints.

Her first real breakthrough came in 1973 on Radio Pakistan with a Sindhi song. From 1977 she was officially a singer there. In the 1990s she also became known outside South Asia. She has toured the world since 1993, and has performed at the Royal Albert Hall in London and at the Holland Festival in Amsterdam in 2014, among other venues. Albums such as Chants soufis du Pakistan from 1995 and Visal from 2002 brought her music to a Western audience. She sings in Urdu, Sindhi, Punjabi, Arabic and Persian.

Her speciality is the kafi, a solo form with percussion and harmonium, in which she sings poems by Sufi poets. She also sings ghazals, qawwali and classical and semi-classical pieces. She is known for her fiery, powerful voice. In 2012 she received the Hilal-e-Imtiaz, and in 2021 the Nishan-e-Imtiaz, the highest civilian honour in Pakistan. She shows that mystical poetry and pop music can meet on stage.
artiest/abida-parveen.listen: Listen to a kafi by her, for example from Visal, and notice how her voice follows the rhythm of harmonium and percussion and grows ever more intense.

artiest/ac-dc.text:
AC/DC is an Australian rock band, founded in Sydney in November 1973 by the brothers Malcolm and Angus Young, who had come from Scotland with their family as children. They saw the name on an electrical appliance belonging to their sister Margaret: alternating current and direct current, an image for the band's raw energy. The school uniform that Angus wore on stage was also her idea. Malcolm played rhythm guitar, Angus lead. Their older brother George Young produced the first records together with Harry Vanda. In 1974 Bon Scott became the singer.

After the Australian albums High Voltage and T.N.T. (1975) the band signed to Atlantic in 1976 and moved to England. Let There Be Rock (1977) and Highway to Hell (1979) followed. In February 1980 Scott died. The English singer Brian Johnson took his place, and that same year Back in Black appeared, one of the best-selling albums of all time. With The Razors Edge (1990), featuring Thunderstruck, came a new period of success. Malcolm Young stopped in 2014 because of dementia and died three years later. In 2020 Power Up appeared.

AC/DC simply calls its own music rock 'n' roll: short, hard songs built on simple guitar riffs, with a tight, stomping rhythm section. The roots lie in the blues and Australian pub rock. The band had a great influence on British heavy metal bands such as Def Leppard and Saxon. Their riffs are so recognisable that an AC/DC song can often be guessed after just a few notes.
artiest/ac-dc.listen: Listen to Thunderstruck and notice the beginning: Angus Young plays a fast, repeated little figure on a single string. Hear how the band then comes in and slowly builds the song up to full power.

artiest/academy-of-st-martin-in-the-fiel.text:
The Academy of St Martin in the Fields is an English orchestra from London. It was founded by John Churchill, at the time musician at the church of St Martin-in-the-Fields, and by Neville Marriner. The first concert was on 13 November 1959 in that church. It began as a small string orchestra without a conductor. Wind players were added later, and the orchestra now plays repertoire from the Baroque to contemporary music.

The performances of the early years played an important part in the revival of Baroque music in England. Marriner himself played solo parts until 1969 and led the orchestra on recordings until the autumn of 1970. After that he stood in front of the group as conductor. Many records date from that period, such as Concertos For Oboe And Strings from 1965, The Four Seasons from 1970 and Music for the Royal Fireworks / Water Music from 1972. In 1974 László Heltay founded a choir that belonged to the orchestra. The choir and the orchestra together recorded the soundtrack album of Amadeus, from 1984, and the UEFA Champions League Anthem.

In 1993 the orchestra became the first to receive the Queen's Award for Export Achievement. Since 2011 the violinist Joshua Bell has been music director. The orchestra shows that classical music can also reach a large audience through the record industry, and it forms a bridge between the classical world and film music.
artiest/academy-of-st-martin-in-the-fiel.listen: Listen to the orchestra in The Four Seasons and notice the clear, light string sound with which the four concertos are played.

artiest/acda-en-de-munnik.text:
Acda en de Munnik is the duo of Thomas Acda (1967) and Paul de Munnik (1970). They met in 1989 at the Kleinkunstacademie in Amsterdam, the Amsterdam academy for cabaret and song, and made music together there for the first time. Their songs are written for a hall that listens. In doing so they continued in the 1990s the line of kleinkunst, the Dutch cabaret song tradition, which had entered pop in the 1960s with Boudewijn de Groot.

The line-up is sober. Acda plays mainly guitar and sometimes harmonica, De Munnik often piano, and David Middelhoff plays bass and other guitars. In 1997 their first CD appeared, Acda en De Munnik. A year later followed Naar huis. It contains Niet of nooit geweest, their breakthrough, which reached number two in the Top 40. Het regent zonnestralen was the third single from that album. The song did not make the charts, but later grew into their most popular song, in the Top 2000 and on Spotify. They received the Zilveren Harp (1997) and the Radio 2 Mijlpaal Prijs (2013), among other awards.

On 4 March 2014 they announced their farewell. The farewell tour ended on 30 March 2015 in Carré. In 2016 they stood on stage together one more time, and in 2023 they announced that they were carrying on again. Acda en de Munnik showed that a song from the theatre, with a guitar, a piano and words you can follow, can also reach a large radio audience.
artiest/acda-en-de-munnik.listen: Het regent zonnestralen tells the story of a character, Herman. Listen to how the song is built like a little story with a main character, and how guitar and piano leave room for the voice, as in kleinkunst.

artiest/ace-of-base.text:
Ace of Base is a Swedish pop group from Gothenburg, made up of the brother and sisters Jonas, Linn and Jenny Berggren and Ulf Ekberg. In 1987 Jonas started a band with two friends, and his sisters joined as singers. Under names such as Tech-Noir they played techno tracks, inspired by Italo disco and house. In 1990 Ekberg joined. Because a Jamaican reggae band was in the studio next to theirs, they began to mix reggae and pop, and that became their own sound. The name Ace of Base came from the Motörhead song Ace of Spades and from their studio, their base.

Swedish record companies turned the group down, but the Danish label Mega Records released Wheel of Fortune in 1992, a hit in Denmark. Producer Denniz PoP then worked on All That She Wants, which caught on all over Europe and later in America. The debut album Happy Nation (1992) appeared in America in adapted form as The Sign, and became one of the best-selling debut albums ever. The title song The Sign spent six weeks at number 1 in America, and Don't Turn Around also became a hit. The Bridge (1995), with Lucky Love and Beautiful Life, followed, and Flowers (1998), released in America as Cruel Summer.

Ace of Base made danceable Europop with reggae rhythms and simple, often cheerful lyrics. After ABBA and Roxette it is the most successful group from Sweden. With producers such as Denniz PoP and the young Max Martin, the group belongs to the beginning of the Swedish pop factory that in the 1990s would go on to make hits for the whole world.
artiest/ace-of-base.listen: Listen to The Sign and notice the rhythm: a dance beat with the emphasis on the offbeat, as in reggae. Hear how the synthesizers and the cool harmonies of the Berggren sisters make that rhythm almost sunny.

artiest/ada-jones.text:
Ada Jones was an English-American singer from the early days of recorded music. She was born in Lancashire in 1873 and moved with her family to Philadelphia when she was six. As early as the 1880s she was on stage as a child. She sang as an alto, learned her songs by ear and could not read music or play an instrument.

In 1893 and 1894 she recorded for Edison Records on wax cylinders. This made her one of the first women to be recorded. After that her recording career collapsed when one of her record companies disappeared. She did not return to the studio until 1905. Her repertoire consisted of ballads, ragtime, vaudeville and comic songs in all kinds of dialects. She sang together with Billy Murray, Cal Stewart, Len Spencer and the American Quartet, among others. She also recorded duets with her daughter Sheilah. Travelling and performing became difficult for her because of epilepsy.

In 1909 she recorded The Yama Yama Man with the Victor Light Opera Company. It became the most popular song of her career and a bestseller. She died in North Carolina in 1922. Her recordings let us hear how pop music sounded in the days when the public still listened to a gramophone with a horn, and singers then had to put comedy and theatre above all into their voices.
artiest/ada-jones.listen: Listen to The Yama Yama Man and notice how clearly she sings and how the song is performed almost like a scene from a play.

artiest/adam-makowicz.text:
Adam Makowicz is a Polish pianist and composer who plays jazz and classical music. He was born Adam Matyszkowicz in 1940 in Hnojník, in the Silesian border region that now lies in the Czech Republic. He grew up in Poland and studied classical music at the Chopin Conservatoire in Kraków. Under the communist regime, freedom and improvisation were not looked upon kindly. Even so, he chose modern jazz and became a touring jazz pianist, with a regular spot in a basement club in Kraków.

In 1977 he made a ten-week tour of the United States, organised by John Hammond. He then recorded a solo album for CBS and settled in New York. In the 1980s, after the imposition of martial law, he was not allowed to travel to Poland. Later he moved to Toronto. His records include Winter Flowers from 1978, The Name Is Makowicz from 1983, Naughty Baby from 1987 and Reflections on Chopin from 2003. He recorded more than thirty albums.

Makowicz makes his own arrangements of Chopin, Gershwin, Berlin, Kern and Porter. He played with major symphony orchestras in Warsaw, Moscow, Washington and London. His playing is known for finesse, inventiveness and technical virtuosity. He shows that jazz and classical music can speak the same language, and he built bridges between worlds that politics had long kept apart.
artiest/adam-makowicz.listen: Listen to his Plays Gershwin or another Gershwin piece and notice how a familiar melody becomes, in his hands, a jazz piano number with turns of its own.

artiest/adelaide-hall.text:
Adelaide Hall was an American jazz singer and entertainer who later lived in England. She was born in 1901 in Brooklyn, New York, and began her career in 1921 in the chorus of the Broadway musical Shuffle Along. It was an enormous success and gave her career a push. She then sang in other Black revues, such as Runnin' Wild in 1923. In 1925 she travelled through Europe with the revue Chocolate Kiddies, with songs by Duke Ellington. In Berlin she also sang at the Eldorado Café.

Her best-known recording she made in 1927 with the orchestra of Duke Ellington: Creole Love Call. She sang no words in it, but used her voice as an instrument alongside the horns. The record became a worldwide hit and brought both Hall and Ellington to a large audience. She also recorded with Fats Waller and performed with artists such as Art Tatum, Louis Armstrong and Cab Calloway. After 1938 she lived in England, where she continued to perform well into the twentieth century.

Her career lasted more than seventy years, from 1921 until her death in 1993. In 2003 she was listed in the Guinness Book of World Records as the artist who had released records in eight consecutive decades. She was an important figure of the Harlem Renaissance and shows how early jazz could turn the voice into an instrument.
artiest/adelaide-hall.listen: Listen to Creole Love Call and notice how her wordless singing joins in with the horns of the orchestra like an extra instrument.

artiest/adele.text:
Adele Adkins was born in 1988 in Tottenham in London and grew up with her mother. She had been singing since she was four and, as she puts it herself, became obsessed with voices. In 2006 she finished the BRIT School, a London school for the performing arts. A friend put her demo on Myspace, after which the label XL Recordings approached her. She wrote her first single, Hometown Glory, when she was sixteen, about her own neighbourhood in London.

Her debut album 19 (2008), named after her age when she wrote most of the songs, contained Chasing Pavements and a version of Make You Feel My Love by Bob Dylan. In 2009 she won the Grammy for Best New Artist. The second album, 21 (2011), came out of a broken relationship and became a worldwide success, with Rolling in the Deep, Someone Like You and Set Fire to the Rain. The album won six Grammys. The Bond theme Skyfall (2012), with which she won an Oscar, followed, and then the albums 25 (2015), with Hello, and 30 (2021), with Easy on Me.

Adele sings with a full mezzo-soprano and writes personal, sensitive songs about love and loss. Critics counted 19 as blue-eyed soul; on 21 there were also influences from American country and roots music. Her songs are often sparsely arranged, so that the voice is at the centre. That she became one of the best-selling artists of the 21st century in this way shows that a classically built song with a strong singer can still reach the whole world.
artiest/adele.listen: Listen to Someone Like You and notice the accompaniment: only a piano that keeps playing the same broken-chord pattern. Hear how Adele sings higher and fuller in the chorus while the piano simply carries on.

artiest/adriaan-willaert.text:
Adriaan Willaert was a Flemish composer of the High Renaissance. He was born around 1490, near Roeselare or in Bruges. According to his pupil Gioseffo Zarlino he first went to Paris to study law, but chose music there and studied with Jean Mouton. Around 1515 he arrived in Rome. He then worked at the court of the Este family in Ferrara. His early style closely resembles that of Josquin des Prez: flowing polyphony, equal voices and a great deal of imitation or strict canon.

In 1527 he became maestro di cappella of San Marco in Venice. He held that post until his death in 1562. Composers from all over Europe came to study with him, and he set high standards for singing and composition. Among other works he wrote the Missa Mente Tota, a Mass in double canon based on a motet by Josquin. His music can be heard on recent recordings such as Musica Nova: The Motets and Missa Mente tota & Motets.

Willaert was one of the northern composers who brought the polyphonic Franco-Flemish style to Italy. He is regarded as the founder of the Venetian school. In this way he stands at the beginning of a line that runs through the choral music of San Marco and prepared the way for later Venetian masters. For the understanding of Western music history he is thus a link between Netherlandish polyphony and the Italian Baroque.
artiest/adriaan-willaert.listen: Listen to a motet by Willaert on Musica Nova: The Motets and notice how the voices take up the same melody in turn and flow through one another.

artiest/adrian-utley.text:
Adrian Utley is an English guitarist, composer and producer, born in 1957 in Northampton. In the mid-1980s he moved to Bristol. He was mad about jazz and played guitar in the band of Big John Patton and with Art Blakey's Jazz Messengers. He collected old instruments and studio equipment and began to concentrate on production and film work. Besides guitar he plays bass, piano and Moog synthesizer, and writes arrangements for brass and strings.

He is best known as a member of Portishead, the Bristol band that began in 1990. The debut Dummy appeared in 1994, followed by Portishead in 1997 and Third in 2008. In the years between the second and third records Utley produced Out of Season by Beth Gibbons and Rustin' Man and worked with Geoff Barrow as Jimi Entley Sound and Fuzzface. He also recorded with Jeff Beck, Marianne Faithfull and Perfume Genius.

Utley also wrote film music. In 2010, together with Will Gregory of Goldfrapp, he made a new soundtrack for the silent film The Passion of Joan of Arc, performed by an orchestra of 23 musicians. In 2013 he played Terry Riley's In C with an ensemble of four organs and nineteen guitars. In this way he brought together the jazz of his youth and the dark, cinematic atmosphere of trip hop, and showed how broadly a guitarist can think.
artiest/adrian-utley.listen: Listen to Arcadia (Music From the Motion Picture) and notice what atmosphere the guitar and the electronic sounds conjure up together.

artiest/adrian-vandenberg.text:
Adrian Vandenberg, whose real name is Adriaan van den Berg, was born in 1954 in The Hague. He grew up in Rotterdam and Enschede, where as a teenager he started his first rock band. He then played in a blues band and in 1977 founded the blues rock group Teaser while studying at the art academy in Arnhem. In 1981 he was invited to audition for Thin Lizzy, but he first finished his studies.

Around 1981 he started his own band, Vandenberg. The debut album was recorded in Jimmy Page's studio, and the ballad Burning Heart became a hit in the Netherlands and also in the United States and Japan. The band toured with Kiss and Ozzy Osbourne, among others. David Coverdale of the British hard rock band Whitesnake asked him several times to join his group. In 1986 Vandenberg disbanded his band and went to Whitesnake. He played the guitar solo on the number 1 hit Here I Go Again and co-wrote Slip of the Tongue and Restless Heart. In 2013 he started the band Vandenberg's MoonKings.

Vandenberg plays melodic hard rock, with layered guitar parts and harmonies, and his great example is Jimi Hendrix. He is also a painter and designed the covers of his own albums himself. With Whitesnake he became one of the few Dutch rock guitarists with a permanent place in a major international band.
artiest/adrian-vandenberg.listen: Listen to Burning Heart by Vandenberg and notice the guitars: several layers that complement one another and together form harmonies. Hear how the ballad starts quietly and works towards a powerful chorus.

artiest/adriana-caselotti.text:
Adriana Caselotti was born in 1916 in Bridgeport, Connecticut, into an Italian-American family. Her father taught music and was a vocal coach, her mother was a coloratura soprano. She herself worked briefly as a chorus girl and session singer at MGM. In 1935 Walt Disney chose her as the voice of Snow White, the title heroine of Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs, Disney's first feature-length animated film.

The film came out in 1937, with songs such as I'm Wishing and Someday My Prince Will Come. Whistle While You Work belongs to the same film. Caselotti received a total of 970 dollars for her work and her name was not in the credits. Afterwards she found it hard to get other work, because Disney did not want to dilute the voice of Snow White. She did, uncredited, still sing the voice of Julia in The Wizard of Oz from 1939, in the Tin Man's song, and in It's a Wonderful Life from 1946.

Her singing is light and clear, trained in the operatic tradition of her parental home. In 1972 she sang I'm Wishing again together with Julie Andrews, and in 1990 she recorded the song once more for the wishing well at Disneyland. In 1994 she became a Disney Legend, the first female voice actor to do so. She died in 1997 in Los Angeles. She shows how an animated film in the 1930s also needed a new kind of singer.
artiest/adriana-caselotti.listen: Listen to Whistle While You Work and notice how the chorus, the whistled melody and the light singing together set down a working rhythm. Try to hear how the arrangement makes the song sound like a chore that does itself.

artiest/aerosmith.text:
Aerosmith was formed in Boston in 1970. Guitarist Joe Perry and bassist Tom Hamilton were already playing together when singer Steven Tyler and drummer Joey Kramer joined. In 1971 guitarist Brad Whitford completed the line-up. Tyler and Perry wrote most of the songs together.

After the debut Aerosmith (1973) and Get Your Wings (1974) the band broke through with Toys in the Attic (1975) and Rocks (1976). Sweet Emotion, Dream On and Walk This Way became hits, and at the end of the 1970s Aerosmith was among the most popular hard rock bands in the world. Drugs and quarrels then led to Perry and Whitford leaving, and the success faded. In 1984 they came back, but the real comeback did not follow until 1986, when the band recorded a new version of Walk This Way with the rap group Run-DMC. With Permanent Vacation (1987), Pump (1989) and Get a Grip (1993) the band was once again as big as before. In 1998 they had their first number 1 with I Don't Want to Miss a Thing.

The music of Aerosmith is hard rock with roots in the blues, later supplemented with pop rock, heavy metal and rhythm and blues. Tyler's raw voice and Perry's riffs form the core. Their comeback is regarded as one of the most striking in rock history. Aerosmith is the best-selling American hard rock band of all time. In 2024 the band stopped touring after Tyler had damaged his voice.
artiest/aerosmith.listen: Listen to Walk This Way in Aerosmith's 1975 version. Notice Joe Perry's guitar riff and how Steven Tyler delivers the verses fast and half spoken, almost like a rapper.

artiest/africa-70.text:
Africa 70 was the band of the Nigerian musician Fela Kuti, the founder of Afrobeat. Kuti began in London, where in the 1960s he studied music and played a mix of jazz and highlife with Koola Lobitos. In 1969 he went with the group to Los Angeles for ten months. There he came into contact with the Black Power movement, which changed his music and his thinking profoundly. After the return to Nigeria the band was given the name Africa '70, and the lyrics were no longer about love but about social problems. Drummer and musical director was Tony Allen.

The group recorded dozens of records in the 1970s, such as Shakara in 1972, Gentleman in 1973, Confusion in 1974 and Zombie in 1976. Kuti founded the Kalakuta Republic, a commune and studio that declared itself independent of the military government. Zombie sharply criticised the Nigerian soldiers. The army then raided the commune. Kuti was badly beaten and his mother was fatally injured.

Afrobeat combines jazz, funk, highlife and Yoruba music, with long tracks and a fixed rhythmic foundation. Allen's drumming was of great importance in this. The music of Africa 70 showed that pop music could also be a political weapon, and it influenced many later musicians in and outside Africa.
artiest/africa-70.listen: Listen to Zombie and notice how the rhythm section holds a tight pattern while horns and vocals answer it.

artiest/afrika-bambaataa.text:
Afrika Bambaataa was actually called Lance Taylor and was born on 17 April 1957 in the Bronx, the child of Jamaican and Barbadian immigrants. His mother had a large and varied record collection. As a boy he became a leader within the street gang the Black Spades. A trip to Africa changed his outlook on the world. He took the name of the Zulu chief Bhambatha and founded the Universal Zulu Nation, an organisation that was meant to get young people out of the gangs through music, dance and art.

In the mid-1970s, inspired by Kool Herc, he organised block parties in the Bronx and became one of the best-known DJs in the neighbourhood. He played everything that was danceable and helped invent the breakbeat style of DJing. He also founded rap groups, such as Soulsonic Force. In 1982 he released Planet Rock with producer Arthur Baker and Soulsonic Force. It featured a melody from Kraftwerk's Trans-Europe Express, rhythms from their track Numbers and a Roland TR-808 drum machine.

Planet Rock laid the foundation for electro-funk, a blend of electronic sounds and hip hop. That same year Bambaataa went with dancers, artists and DJs on the first hip hop tour outside America, and so he spread hip hop culture around the world. In 2016 he stepped down as leader of the Zulu Nation following accusations of child sexual abuse, and in 2025 he lost a civil case over them. He died on 9 April 2026.
artiest/afrika-bambaataa.listen: Listen to Planet Rock (1982). Notice the cool synthesizer melody from Kraftwerk and the dry claps of the 808 drum machine, and hear how the rappers get a party going on top of them.

artiest/afrika-bambaataa-en-soulsonic-fo.text:
Afrika Bambaataa & Soulsonic Force was the group of DJ and producer Afrika Bambaataa, born Lance Taylor in the Bronx in New York. As a boy he was a leader in the street gang the Black Spades. After a trip to Africa his outlook on the world changed. He took the name of the Zulu leader Bhambatha and founded the Universal Zulu Nation, a movement that wanted to get young people out of the gangs through music, dance and graffiti. From 1977 he organised block parties in the South Bronx. There, rap groups emerged around him, such as Soulsonic Force with the rappers Mr. Biggs, Pow Wow and Emcee G.L.O.B.E.

Bambaataa listened not only to funk and soul, but also to Kraftwerk and Yellow Magic Orchestra. In 1982 the group gave up the live band and switched entirely to electronics. With producer Arthur Baker and synthesizer player John Robie they made Planet Rock. They used the Roland TR-808 drum machine, the melody of Trans-Europe Express and drum patterns from Kraftwerk's Numbers, and blended it with funk and rap. The track became a club hit and laid the foundation for electro.

Planet Rock linked German electronic music with the hip hop of New York and influenced later styles such as house, techno and Miami bass. In 1982 Bambaataa also took hip hop on the first international hip hop tour. His name was later severely damaged by accusations of sexual abuse, after which he stepped down in 2016 as leader of the Zulu Nation. He died in 2026.
artiest/afrika-bambaataa-en-soulsonic-fo.listen: Listen to Planet Rock from 1982. Can you hear the melody of Trans-Europe Express by Kraftwerk? Also notice the hard, dry claps of the TR-808 drum machine beneath the raps.
